==English== {{swp}} ===Pronunciation=== * {{IPA|en|/ˈbɪl/|[ˈbɪɫ]}} ** {{audio|en|en-us-bill.ogg|a=US}} ** {{audio|en|En-uk-the bill.ogg|a=UK|text=the bill}} *** {{IPA|en|/ˈbɪʊ̯/|[ˈbɪʊ̯]|a=l-vocalization}} * {{rhymes|en|ɪl|s=1}} * {{hyph|en|bill}} * {{hmp|en|Bill}} ===Etymology 1=== {{etymid|en|document-themed}} From {{inh|en|enm|bille}}, from {{der|en|xno|bille|}}, from {{der|en|fro|bulle|}}, from {{der|en|la-med|bulla||seal, sealed document}}. {{dbt|en|bull#Etymology 2|t1=papal bull; bubble|bulla}}. ====Noun==== {{en-noun}} # A written list or inventory. {{n-g|(Now obsolete except in specific senses or set phrases; [[bill of lading]], [[bill of goods]], etc.)}} # A document, originally sealed; a formal statement or official memorandum. {{n-g|(Now obsolete except with certain qualifying words; [[bill of health]], [[bill of sale]] etc.)}} # {{senseid|en|draft law}} A [[draft]] of a [[law]], [[present]]ed to a [[legislature]] for [[enactment]]; a [[propose]]d or [[project]]ed law. #: {{syn|en|measure}} #: {{ux|en|Mr. Speaker, on behalf of the Prime Minister, I beg to introduce a '''bill''' entitled{{...}}}} #* {{RQ:Shakespeare Merry Wives|II|I|line=28|text=Why, I'll exhibit a '''bill''' in the parliament for the putting down of men.}} # {{lb|en|obsolete|law}} A [[declaration]] made in writing, stating some [[wrong]] the [[complainant]] has [[suffer]]ed from the [[defendant]], or a [[fault]] [[commit]]ted by some person against a law. #* {{RQ:Dickens Bleak House|text=... the legion of '''bills''' in the suit have been transformed into mere bills of mortality ...|1}} # {{senseid|en|banknote}}{{lb|en|US|Canada}} A piece of paper [[money]]; a [[banknote]]. #* {{quote-book|en|year=1830|author=Anon|title=The Galaxy of Wit: Or, Laughing Philosopher, Being a Collection of Choice Anecdotes, Many of Which Originated in or about "The Literary Emporium"|passage=He gave the change for a three dollar '''bill'''. Upon examination, the '''bill''' proved to be counterfeit.}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1935|year_published=19 March 2014|title=Cabins in the Laurel|page=231|isbn= 9781469620770|publisher=University of North Carolina Press|url=https://www.google.co.nz/books/edition/Cabins_in_the_Laurel/4WSVAwAAQBAJ|passage={{...}}So I wropped 'em up in a five dollar '''bill''' and tied 'em up and sent 'em, and they ain't back yet.”}} ## {{lb|en|slang|North America}} One [[hundred]] [[dollar]]s. ##* {{quote-book|en|title={{w|Skin Tight (novel)|Skin Tight}}|passage=All we got from her was Stranahan's location, and barely that. A house in the bay, she said. A house with a windmill. Easiest five '''bills''' that woman ever made.|year=1989|author=w:Carl Hiaasen|page=113|isbn=9781101436639|publisher=w:Penguin Group}} # {{lb|en|slang|UK}} One [[hundred]] [[pound sterling|pounds sterling]]. #*: In the conversation Henshall says he {{sic}} "struggling to find people to go up the roads" explaining how it would be "no good for black people" and how they need a "young white boy to go up there".
Stock agrees, saying how he knows "this kid" who "owes me 12 '''bills'''". # {{senseid|en|invoice}} A written note of goods sold, [[service]]s [[render]]ed, or work done, with the price or [[charge]] owing; an [[invoice]]. #: {{ux|en|He received a '''bill''' of £9 for the groceries.}} #: {{syn|en|account|invoice}} #* {{RQ:Shakespeare Timon of Athens|III|IV|line=85|text=My lord, here is my '''bill'''.}} # {{senseid|en|receipt}} {{lb|en|slang|India}} A written note of goods sold, [[service]]s [[render]]ed, or work done, listing the price or [[charge]] paid; a [[receipt]]. # {{senseid|en|advertisement}} A paper, written or printed, and [[post]]ed up or given away, to advertise something, as a lecture, a play, or the sale of goods #: {{syn|en|broadsheet|broadside|card|circular|flier|flyer|handbill|poster|posting| placard| notice|throwaway}} #* {{RQ:Shakespeare Midsummer|I|II|line=104|text=In the meantime I will draw a '''bill''' of properties, such as our play wants.}} # A [[writing]] that [[bind]]s the [[signer]] or signers to pay a [[certain]] [[sum]] at a [[future]] day or on [[demand]], with or without [[interest]], as may be [[state]]d in the [[document]]; a [[bill of exchange]]. In the United States, it is usually called a [[note]], a note of hand, or a [[promissory note]]. #: {{syn|en|bank bill|banker's bill|bank note|banknote|Federal Reserve note|government note|greenback|note}} #* {{RQ:Shakespeare Merry Wives|I|I|line=8|text=Ay, and Rato-lorum too; and a gentleman born, Master Parson; who writes himself Armigero, in any '''bill''', warrant, quittance, or obligation, Armigero.}} # A set of items presented together. #: {{ux|en|We've got a brilliant new comedian on the '''bill''' tonight.}} #* {{RQ:Guardian|date=June 26, 2017|author=Alexis Petridis| title=Glastonbury 2017 verdict: Radiohead, Foo Fighters, Lorde, Stormzy and more| url=https://www.theguardian.com/music/2017/jun/26/glastonbury-2017-verdict-radiohead-foo-fighters-lorde-stormzy-and-more| passage=Meanwhile, the '''bills''' on the main stages skewed towards mainstream pop, with mixed results. Lorde’s Friday evening Other stage appearance was one of the weekend’s highlights. The staging and choreography were fantastic – a giant glass tank on a hydraulic platform, in and around which a troupe of dancers acted out the highs and lows of a teenage party|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20261012112015/https://www.theguardian.com/music/2017/jun/26/glastonbury-2017-verdict-radiohead-foo-fighters-lorde-stormzy-and-more|archivedate=12 October 2026}} # {{lb|en|UK|{{w|Eton College}}}} A [[list]] of [[pupil]]s to be [[discipline]]d for [[break]]ing [[school]] [[rule]]s. #* {{quote-book|en|year=1875|author=Sir H. Perhaps from a special use of {{cog|ang|bil}}, {{m|ang|bill|t=hook; sword}} (see below). ====Noun==== {{en-noun}} # {{senseid|en|Q31528}} {{lb|en|zootomy}} The [[beak]] of a [[bird]], especially when [[small]] or [[flattish]]; sometimes also used with reference to a [[platypus]], [[turtle]], or other [[animal]]. #: {{syn|en|beak|neb|nib|pecker}} #* {{RQ:Shakespeare Midsummer|III|I|line=125|text=The woosel cock so black of hue, With orange-tawny '''bill''', The throstle with his note so true, The wren with little quill{{...}}}} #* {{RQ:en:New York Times|author=w:Olivia Judson| title=The hemiparasite season [print version: Under the hemiparasite, ''International New York Times'', 24–25 December 2014, page 7]| url=http://www.nytimes.com/2014/12/24/opinion/the-hemiparasite-season.html| archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20141223181330/https://www.nytimes.com/2014/12/24/opinion/the-hemiparasite-season.html| archivedate=23 December 2014| date=23 December 2014| passage={{...}} The flesh [of the [[mistletoe]] berry] is sticky, and forms strings and ribbons between my thumb and forefinger. For the mistletoe, this viscous goop – and by the way, viscous comes to English from {{l|la|viscum}} – is crucial. The stickiness means that, after eating the berries, birds often regurgitate the seeds and then wipe their '''bills''' on twigs – leading to the seeds' getting glued to the tree, where they can germinate and begin the cycle anew.}} # {{senseid|en|beaklike projection, especially a promontory}} A [[beaklike]] [[projection]], especially a [[promontory]]. #: {{ux|en|There is a lighthouse on
